newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria oil refinery seeks new credits.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria oil refinery seeks new credits.

text.p: Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery, Neftochim, hopes to negotiate an increase in its credit from France's Paribas bank branch in Geneva, a refinery spokeswoman said on Friday.

Tatyana Hadzhieva said Neftochim's finance director Atanas Zaikov had left for Switzerland to negotiate an increase of an existing $50 million credit line for purchasing crude to combat the country's fuel crisis.
Plant officials said Netherland's ING Bank had also renewed a credit line to the refinery.
Credits to Neftochim from the two banks total $70 million to date, they said.
The refinery at the Black Sea port of Bourgas is the main fuel supplier to the domestic market. The plant owes millions of dollars to crude suppliers mainly as a result of unrealistically low prices.
The interim government, which took office in mid-February, has raised petrol prices twice by up to 178 percent and by up to 10 percent in line with the lev/dollar exchange rate and inflation.

Hadzhieva quoted Neftochim's executive director Nikola Karagyozov as saying at a news conference in Bourgas on Thursday that the increased prices would help the plant start paying some of its debts to suppliers.
The new prices are based on an exchanged rate of 2045 levs to the dollar, Karagyozov said.
The lev has firmed to 1,700 to the dollar in recent days from a record low of 3,000 three weeks ago. Traders ascribe the rise to low foreign currency demand.

The refinery has raised daily distribution volumes of diesel for the domestic market, easing the month-long fuel crisis. The plant distributed 3,100 tonnes of diesel and 1,322 tonnes of petrol on Thursday and has 86,000 tonnes of crude on stock. -- Liliana Semerdjieva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
